references.text: The prophet Isaiah predicts that the Messiah will be buried with the rich, which is fulfilled in Mark 15:46 when Joseph of Arimathea, a wealthy man, buries Jesus in his own new tomb.
Psalm 34:20 speaks of not a bone being broken, which is relevant because it refers to how Jesus' body was treated at the burial with care and without further harm, as described in Mark 15:46.
In John 19:40-42 it is also described how Jesus was taken down from the cross, wrapped in linen, and laid in a tomb, which is a direct parallel to Mark 15:46.
Matthew 27:59-60 gives a parallel account of how Joseph of Arimathea took down Jesus' body, wrapped it in clean linen, and placed it in his new tomb, which corresponds directly with Mark 15:46.
Luke 23:53 also tells how Jesus was taken down from the cross, wrapped in linen, and laid in a tomb cut out of rock, which is a direct parallel to Mark 15:46.
